summary: Implement scoped reads/views, first Office legal connection, durable KDS and single-payment recovery, bounded reads/proof metadata and native resource cleanup. Real independent Auth/JWT REST, first/additional store registration with Auth worker and Office mapping, and POS private Storage are exercised in isolated development fixtures. Full business/browser/domain adoption, mixed/12h trials and production remain incomplete.
businessInvariants: Preserve existing 50% menu quota reservation/cancel restoration and immutable deferred-order allocations; do not modify the original payment/promotion allocator.
Backward compatible live-event INSERT still invalidates legacy clients; new clients merge bounded changed IDs from INSERT and UPDATE signals.
Read scope switches, disposal and late errors cannot restore another store; confirmed writes are distinct from subsequent refresh state.
Original user workspace and unrelated Excel work remain intact; G0–G7/soak completion stays false until actual evidence exists.
The first internal POS legal entity can connect with zero stores, using independent Auth and explicit Office ownership confirmation. External entities retain the existing unsupported policy.
Each DB transaction is atomic and cross-DB completion is a recoverable operation, never a claimed distributed transaction; proof expires and is never an Auth/service credential.

Persist each new KDS item-progress identity before HTTP; a prepared or ambiguous record cannot become a fresh handoff. Preserve existing quantities, floor/checker routing and native command idempotency.
Resolve both direct event UUIDs and JeonGabok private batch request UUIDs by original active actor/store. Never grant clients direct access to the private batch action table.
Keep new progress journals invisible to legacy clients, preserve original intent order, and retain confirmed writes despite failed cleanup, refresh or later assignment change.

Confirmed cashier item mutations remain confirmed after failed follow-up reads; their original view cannot load/apply another active store or a later assignment. QC follow-up writes preserve the active filter and never return an old store after navigation/disposal.

Application/Auth/Storage schema fixtures are source-hashed, private, owned and network-isolated; clone no production business rows, password hashes, file objects or cron schedules. Bucket reference configuration is separate. Candidate migration success never means production applied, whole-plan complete or twelve-hour PASS.

Root-bound client scope tracks trusted actor/role/legal/store/access changes and every A-B-A generation; token/display/loading changes do not trigger data reloads. Twenty-three FutureProvider reads reject blocked sessions and discard prior generations; QC follow-up/issue state is disposed on scope changes. Server RLS remains authoritative; other legacy notifiers and uncertain commands remain unfinished.

Additive single-payment receipts serialize the original actor/operation identity, reject payload reuse, retain immutable native payment results and recheck current actor/store permissions on replay/read. Existing process_payment and combined/non-revenue native definitions, money, stock and invoice semantics stay unchanged. New API is not yet connected to durable cashier intent/UI.
Current user_accessible_stores returns scalar UUIDs; explicit positional aliases preserve both scalar and named fixture compatibility. No candidate migration has been applied to production.

Pinned owned fixture supautils crashes on denied function execution even without candidate/schema changes. PGOPTIONS disables only cosmetic GRANT hints; actual anonymous ACL denial, protected tables and native financial execution remain checked. Never change production settings or report this as a reproduced production engine failure.

Settings/report notifier and widget view lifetimes reset and reload on real actor/store/access changes. Confirmed setting saves remain true after navigation/disposal, stale reads cannot undo saves, clearing nullable charges clears UI, and same-scope refresh preserves unsaved controls. PIN follow-up steps and toasts stay in the original widget view. Remaining legacy commands, strict PIN read outcomes and file/resource budgets are not claimed complete.

Dispose the native JSON worker owned by each temporary KDS PostgrestClient, not just HTTP. Bound full RPC and cleanup budgets; cleanup failure cannot change a confirmed command or replace the original uncertainty/error. Payment-proof HTTP/JSON cleanup uses the same rule. No DB operation, new query/retry, physical adapter or production setting is added by this resource fix. Linux native VM measurements do not establish browser/night or physical-device improvement.

A cashier full payment persists its original actor/store/order/version/amount/method before HTTP. Only the atomic sending owner may charge. Unknown delivery blocks alternative methods; reconciliation never resubmits. A server cancellation barrier defeats late original delivery, while already committed receipts stay confirmed. Full intent cannot become a stale partial charge. SQLite/IndexedDB fail closed, never evict unknown records, and preserve confirmed results through cleanup failure. Split/combined/non-revenue durable recovery and SQL batching remain incomplete.

Owned runtime uses new private JWT/passwords and real Auth Admin API accounts, independent native DBs, authenticator JWT role switching, and unmodified Office Edge. Loopback routing never forwards missing/wrong project keys, private schemas or unprepared services. A physical lost ACK preserves original operation despite observed Deno transport replay; neither elapsed time nor unprepared Storage/Realtime/physical hardware is faked.

New law/brand/first and additional stores use real registration APIs and the unmodified store-account-onboarding Edge with real GoTrue Admin writes. Shared brand accounts are reconciled, not duplicated. Actual opening readiness and zero active employees remain blocked rather than being seeded as successful physical handover/business readiness.

Native two-project first/additional-store fixture now exercises actual initial-password Edge, generation trigger, new employees, POS private Storage and eight photo attendance events with cross-store denial. Synthetic JPEG is decoded by the real Dart image library; no physical camera/hardware, whole lifecycle or production claim.

nPlusOne.reason: KDS receipt recovery is set-based; commands retain domain RPCs and are not disguised as parallel lookup work. Existing item/batch writers remain in scope for the later whole-flow audit. Schema metadata is captured in bounded identity batches, with preaggregated dependency joins; no per-object remote calls. Payment receipts use one original business command and one optional lookup for <=100 IDs; legacy split-payment per-part calls are still unfinished and are not represented as fixed. JSON lifetime fixes add zero remote calls; the measured gateway still sends 101 calls including warmup for 100 reads. Existing payment-proof per-queued-file metadata lookup still needs the later batch-path review; cleanup is not represented as solving it. Proof flushing selects at most 10 eligible files, preloads only id/tax_entity_id for distinct stores in one <=10-row/64-KiB request, and retains existing object paths. Per-object upload/sign/attach remains necessary bounded serial storage work, not a claimed set-based storage API. Same-actor simultaneous flushes share one pending future. Actor changes stop subsequent physical sends; original JWT headers are captured for RPC/storage. No persistent store metadata cache is added. Single payment is one native transactional RPC, no item loop; receipt lookup is bounded at 100. Each RPC owns a 15s/512KiB response budget (plus separate <=2s JSON cleanup), never retries a charge, and freezes original Auth/params. Local financial ledger is separate, <=100 records/256KiB, <=8KiB per record, with one native worker per ledger and <=100 queued requests; SQLite busy wait <=2s per lock, native DB <=256 pages. Multi-step partial/combined SQL paths remain unfinished.
